title: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
objective: I can plot ordered pairs in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane.
model: four-quadrant plane with the sign pattern of each quadrant: I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −)

widgets.component: slide a point to 5 units left of 0 and to −3 + 6; ordered pair for 2 right 5 up; which number moves left or right
widgets.root: Slider keys −5 and 3 and pair (2, 5) verified. The two slider items review the number line (7-2) rather than the lesson's own warm-up, which is on rectangles.

widgets.component: quadrant of (−4, 5), sign pattern for +x, −y, point on the x-axis, sort six pairs into four quadrants, 'x is −2 so I move DOWN' error
widgets.root: All sort cards land in the right quadrant ((3, 4) I, (−2, 5) II, (−6, −1) III, (1, −3) IV, (−4, 2) II, (5, −6) IV); error step e=1 is the first wrong step.

widgets.component: signs and quadrant of five points, quadrant to sign pattern, (−5, 3) moved 8 right, swapped-coordinates error
widgets.root: Table (+/−/IV, −/−/III, 0/+/y-axis, −/+/II, +/0/x-axis), match pairs, (3, 3) and (4, −2) verified. 3.5 repeats the style of 2.1 and 3.6 of 1.3, so §3 adds less new than it appears.

widgets.component: generated quadrant, coordinates and axis identification on a drawn four-quadrant plane
widgets.root: Ran 250 seeds x 4 levels: figure points match the keyed answer in every draw, no point outside the frame. Same generator and levels as 7-5 Practice §4, so these items are identical to 7-5's; they read points, they do not plot them.

widgets.component: plot a named point on the plane
widgets.root: Practice's only plotting task is level 2, which draws a half-plane (x from −e to e with y 0..e, or the reverse): two quadrants at a time, never Quadrant III. The lesson's objective and its watch-me case (−3, −4) are all four quadrants, which only Challenge 3.1 (level 3) reaches.
widgets.replacement: Use act:plot {mode:'point'} at level 3 (full four-quadrant plane) for Practice 4.7 and add a second level-3 instance at the end of §3 so a student plots at least one point in each quadrant before the mastery check; keep the swapped-x/y and wrong-sign traps.

widgets.component: library (−3, 4), park (5, −2), hospital (−4, −1), negative x and y, count points in Quadrant II, y = 0 and x = −7
widgets.root: Keys II, IV, III, III, 3 (of (−4,6), (−7,1), (−9,9)) and 'on the x-axis, 7 units left' verified.

widgets.component: generated axis/quadrant identification, 'start at (−3, 4), move 9 right then 2 down' quadrant
widgets.root: Same generator and checks as §4; L4 move-then-name and 'n units from each axis' samples recomputed.

widgets.component: error analysis (−3, −5); describe a move from Quadrant I to III; a < 0, b < 0; robot path 7 left, 5 up, 3 right, 8 down; charging-pad corners; sensors in Quadrant III or IV; right-then-down into Quadrant IV
widgets.root: Recomputed: robot ends at (−4, −3), Quadrant III; pad corners (5, 3), (−5, 3), (−5, −3), (5, −3) with quadrants I-IV; B, D, G and H make 4 on the drawn plane; 6 right and 4 down from (−5, 3) gives (1, −1).

widgets.where: Challenge 3.1-3.3 (act:plot point L3, polygon L4; match)
widgets.component: plot points in all four quadrants; plot the missing rectangle corners from area or perimeter; match move sets to end points
widgets.root: Level 3 covers all four quadrants; level-4 polygon items are the 7-7 skill reapplied across quadrants; the five move/end pairs are right.

widgets.component: three error analyses (swapped up/down, 'negative means bottom-left', axis point called a quadrant); Mei vs Jamal; (−p, q); (3, −9) up 14; Quadrant III 6 and 4 from the axes; four-quadrant rectangle; sensors on a drawn plane
widgets.root: Error steps (e=1, 2, 2) verified; keys Quadrant III, 5, (−4, −6), the rectangle (−5, 4)...(−5, −2), and N (5, −4) on the drawn plane are right.

formulaOrder.formula: quadrant sign patterns I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −)

typography: Practice 2.1-2.5, 3.1, 3.3-3.6, 5.4 (stems, cards, table rows, steps) and Challenge 2.1-2.3 print coordinates with an ASCII hyphen-minus; match 3.2 prints the sign patterns '(-, +)', '(-, -)', '(+, -)' and the sign-table answers with a hyphen; Challenge 2.5 and the generated items use U+2212.
